utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Good morning to you as well, Mr. Anttila.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you ready to proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Antilla, I would like you to look at a chart, and it's 1D190047, and I would like to bring this up via Sanction, Madam Registrar. Mr. Anttila, just by way of background I was just examining some of the testimony yesterday both from me and from Judge Orie, and I would just like to clarify some of the information transfer to Sector South headquarters and then on to UNMO headquarters in Zagreb, and I have attempted to lay this out --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, could counsel repeat the document number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. It's 1D190047 via Sanction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the way, I notice that I have forgotten, I think for the first time in seven years, to invite Madam Registrar to call the case. It has to be done once, and it -- I should speak to myself about precision.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, if we could just look at this, this -- is it on the screen? I'm sorry. It is on the screen. Okay. Mr. Anttila, just by -- just clarifying your testimony, and you had seven teams that were providing information to you, and you noted for us that they then put together a daily sitrep, situation report, as well as a separate form that we looked at as P65; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: P65 was the form which -- by which they were, for example, reporting the data on villages that they had visited, and then the sitrep -- it's like in the drawing here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And -- but they had a sitrep that they also gave you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sitrep would include findings on the -- of the patrols that would be considered relevant to the situation in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So with regard to the daily sitreps, and I'm looking at the bottom blue line, if a house was burning it would go in that sitrep, but if a house was found burnt it went in the form P65; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could be the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And then from there if we follow the red line an entirely separate situation report with I think you told us not all the information from the team situation reports was sent on a daily basis to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And then on one occasion, I believe we are talking about the document P68, the sitrep reports that you brought out being sent to Zagreb as well as P176, the data population; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I could follow the line of your explanation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, it's -- there was a daily sitrep from the sector to UNMO headquarters, which included the most important information coming from the teams but not all the information coming from the teams, and it was a separate list on the data collected from the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, going back to the bottom, sir, the daily sitrep of the UNMO teams as well as the form, why wasn't that just one document that was provided to you as opposed to two?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm -- I don't understand the question, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On the bottom portion on a daily basis, you've got a daily sitrep from every team that had information concerning burnings, and then you also had a form that we looked at as P65?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you had two forms.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the -- the form P -- which is Exhibit P65, that was a separate task given to the teams to see the villages and see the damages in the area, And that was produced in the form of that form because that way we could keep track of what was covered and what was not covered. So it was not reported on a daily basis; it was reported on -- whenever a certain place was visited. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I will offer the chart into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit D171.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kehoe, there is a difference in the arrows. Some are depicted as apparently being more important than others. The blue are thick; the others are thin. Is there any meaning behind that which has not been explored?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I was attempting to demonstrate some consistency on where one document comes from the other, and I can clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, the daily situation reports that you received on a daily basis, it was from those documents that you produced P68, which is the summary of humanitarian violations, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's coming -- yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the forms that you used in P65, they were in part with other information used to come up with the data compilations in P176; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although that's not fully depicted in the mixed sources, but thank you for this further explanation. D171 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the sake of clarity, I was trying last night with the staff to try to get this as clear as possible for the Chamber. And I will gladly, if Your Honour wants to change it to a different colour such as the arrow up to the right of P76 from yellow to some other color because I believe in fairness to the witness, he said that data compilation is not only made up of the forms but from other information as well. So I can do that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's sufficiently explained at this moment. Colours are not decisive. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might have one moment. [Defence counsel confer].

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, when -- on the form that we are talking about in P176, now if we could go back to the page 1 of P176. If we could go to the next page. I'm sorry. Spin that a bit. If we can leave it -- yeah. That's great. Now, on this sheet, Mr. Anttila, it notes that the definition on the top line of partially damaged, tell me how you define partially damaged.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially damaged would be, you know, something like burned, windows broken in, and things like that; totally damaged would be a house that would be in a condition where it could not give a shelter to a person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But -- and then partially damaged is something that you almost consider to be livable?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's something where you could get cover, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when you were sending people throughout there, there was a degree of subjectivity by the individual UNMOs as to whether something was partially damaged or not, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's obvious, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can stay with this form for one moment, and I would like to turn your attention to, if I may, on this exhibit, and the P number at the top is 8204. If we could go to 00548204, which is two pages up. And I'd like to talk to Gradac, the third from the top from the Sinj team?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this notes as we go across the 70 buildings there and all damaged?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And it notes here that probably from 1992?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you have many inclusions in there of property damage prior to Storm?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's also true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So -- but you never backed those numbers out of the final number on damages, did you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a compiled list of all the damages, not only from Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the document that is entitled here is: "Data on population left in Sector South and destroyed houses after Operation Storm," isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But you included it but didn't back it out?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, well these houses are still -- were still damaged after Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So based on that, sir, we as we go through here don't know -- you're looking at everything that you saw at Operation -- after Operation Storm, and looking at these numbers, we don't know if this was damaged from 1992 to 1995 or sometime after August 1995, to here November of 1995, do we?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The document clearly states which houses were believed to have been destroyed prior to or at some other period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether that should be an objection to the question or just an observation that you exhaust all the information contained in this document is a matter to be seen, but some distinction can be made, Mr. Kehoe, that's clearly from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I think we should -- I will clarify that yet further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can say -- if we can just look at that grid reference that we have on the screen of -- for Gradac is XJ0353. And I ask us to go to -- up to page 00548212. And I asked us to look at Team Sibenik and go down one, two, three, four, five, six, seven -- nine to, again, the village of Gradac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And it's virtually the same grid reference although it's a little tighter being -- as opposed to one kilometre square a hundred metres square, right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, but it is the same area?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you again have 70 residences destroyed, same as the one for the Sinj team when it mentioned Gradac, right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But there's nothing in the comments about this probably being from 1992, is there?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So if we look at this, number one, you would agree that that's double counted?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And number two, there is a discrepancy of the teams whether or not that damage took place after Operation Storm or going back to 1992?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Team Sibenik obviously did not assess that fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, do you know whether these other teams, when they went through and compiled these statistics, failed to assess that fact as well?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Sibenik team has assessed damages on certain villages to be prior to Operation Storm, but I don't have any information on individual villages, how the assessment was made, when the damage was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well -- and you're talking about as you get down that page Team Sibenik did, in fact, make that assessment in other villages?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In other villages, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, clearly this is a disagreement among these -- the teams. Did you, when you were going through this, attempt to reconcile this?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall this individual case, and we tried to tell the teams to be telling us -- giving us the information if the damage would be prior to Operation Storm, but obviously in this case they failed to do that in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, let me talk to you a little bit about a couple of documents and a couple of these villages, and if we may I would like to turn to the second page of this document. If we can flip back to 00548203. And I'd like you to go down about three, four to the page until we come to an insert for Rodaljice under Zadar-Benkovac team, R-o-d-a-l-j-i-c-e, with a grid reference WJ6277. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In in that particular location, you have 701 buildings, 118 destroyed, 230 damaged for a total of 348 buildings damaged and destroyed?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I would like you to examine -- I would like to bring up 1D190006. Now, sir, this is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is from a larger volume. It's a translation from the population census taken by the Republic of Croatia in 1991. It is -- as you can see on the front page, it's population. A portion of it is dwellings and other installations. And if we could just flip it to -- we can go one more page. One more page -- okay -- oops, I'm sorry, maybe it's another one after that. It comes to this -- where in fact the statistics are begin. Now, if we could just blow that up. This is a page concerning dwellings for permanent residences and settlement of persons. Yeah, blow that up. According to the equipment of the dwellings with installations and auxiliary premises. Now, if we could just drift down a little bit to the town of Rodaljice. It is actually the ninth one down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you see that ninth one down?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think it might be -- Your Honour, it might be easier for the witness to look at a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you see Rodaljice on there, Mr. Antilla?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just barely, but yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, under the line of total number of buildings in the village, it notes 43, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you in Rodaljice list 701?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So did you notice a tremendous building surge in that area between 1991 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The evidence already from the witness is that he didn't get to the area until August 4th of 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, if the numbers are so different and if the witness statement says that he used the 1991 population statistics, then the question can be put to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was there a big building surge in this area?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's stay with Rodaljice, and if we can just take this document down from the screen and put up -- I'm going to go back to this document, Judge, so I will move it into evidence after I'm finished with it because there is some other items. If we can put 1D190040, and I have distributed paper copies to everyone in the courtroom. And this is another part of the population census. Now, sir, I would like you to as you page through this go to page 3 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Could we possibly put it on the ELMO to -- for assistance?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is a breakdown of nationalities in individual settlements in 1995, and as we see the breakdown -- excuse me, 1991, I apologise. I stand corrected, for 1991. And if we go to the Rodaljice line, the census reflects that in 1991 there were 162 people living in Rodaljice and 162 were Croats.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in your document you reflect that 348 structures were damaged -- totally damaged or partially damaged in that village?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says on the paper, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now -- and there is nothing in the line for comments if that was done prior to Operation Storm or after Operation Storm, is there?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, based on that, is it your -- the assessment of the UNMOs and human rights teams that the Croats, when coming back in after Operation Storm, did this kind of destruction on the village, a village, where Croats had lived?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no assessment on that. That's merely the numbers that were found out and reported to us about damaged buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when you looked at villages, is it your testimony you never made an assessment as to whether or not this was a Croat village or a Serb village?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could see it on the map that it was obviously a Croat village, but there is no mention -- no remark on that fact, on the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's move up the page. Let's go back to P176, and then we'll flip back to -- if we can go back to P176 and go to 548203. If we can leave this on the ELMO because we'll go back to it. Now, if we go back -- I believe -- that's the page. If you say the -- again the village of Lisane, it's about a quarter of the way down. Do you see that? Lisane by the Zadar-Benkovac?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That was 180 structures?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 140 totally damaged and 20 partially damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. So that's 160 out of 180 structures either partially or completely damaged, right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's go -- and again, before we do that, there is no comment in there that that was prior to Operation Storm, is there?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No because it was our common knowledge that Zadar-Benkovac team was working on the area where there were houses that had been destroyed before Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So is it your testimony that this was destroyed prior to Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information on that fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you just said to us that it was your common knowledge that the "Zadar-Benkovac team was working on the area that there were houses that had been destroyed before Operation Storm." So do we take it from that statement that you just made that everything that is included under Zadar-Benkovac is, for the most part, damage that took place prior to Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After 13 years, based on the information that I have in front of me, I cannot make that assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's go back to the document that's on the ELMO, 1D190041, and we go to that village of Lisane, and in that population sentence -- census, pardon me, of 1991 it reflects that there were 892 residents, 884 national -- 884 all nationalities, 884 Croats, and if we flip all the way over to the right-hand side to get the math straight if we can -- well, take my word for it, it says eight unknown.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just for the sake of clarity, Judge, it's all the way over on the right-hand side. You see the eight unknown, so the math comes back out to 891.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So this village again where your records reflect 160 damaged residences had been a Croatian village prior -- at least in 1991?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And again, you don't know -- well, do you know when this damage occurred in Lisane?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if we look at -- if we would take up the grid reference on the map, you could see the location, And by that then it could be assessed whether it was -- it could have been done before Operation Storm or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And again, that's not reflected in this -- in the other column --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you include it in the overall damage?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's still damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you allow me to ask some clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Either from the witness or that you could give it. The database contains approximately 360 entries, villages or at least geographical entities. That's what we find in the UNMO report. In this report, if I look at the 1991 and the -- then I see 60. So apparently the structure of this report in 1991 on the population and what geographical entities were used by the UNMOs appears to be 106, that's still unclear to me. That could have several explanations, and what the consequences exactly are I can't oversee at this moment, But I am noticing that we are now comparing the data from a 360-entry document with a 60-entry document, approximately 60. That raises all kind of questions in my mind, just for you to be aware of. [Defence counsel confer].

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, you are comparing the -- actually, this particular census on both levels --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- has -- I mean, it's a huge, huge book where every one of these villages is broken down. I have just tried to separate this out. The reason why I've tried to separate this out and give it a more tighter fashion so it's manageable, but if you look at these grid references here, Judge, I mean if we go to -- for instance, and we'll be talking about Korenica. It's a grid reference of a kilometre by a kilometre where the report notes 3.000 buildings in a kilometre-by-kilometre grid reference. Now, I gladly will provide this entire book, but this particular census is very tightly set out village by village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm not saying that we can't draw any conclusions; I just notice that at this moment we are at the one hand looking at a document with a factor-6 multiplier number of entries, and in the other it's different. I don't know how to deal with that, but for me just to try to understand. If it's -- if the whole of the area is covered, I do not even know that. If the total number of population matches or not, I have no opportunity yet to verify that. But that raises all kind of rather problematic arithmetic matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I tried to put this as tightly as possible together and to contrast that with the information that's being presented. Obviously we had some of these villages that in 1991 were virtually a hundred per cent Croatian with showing in this statistical form massive damage. And -- which raises the question of course not only when it took place, putting aside the question of did the Croats when they all come back, destroy their own houses? That's contrary to what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, or that Serbs had taken over the houses and those were destroyed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All kind of questions. I just want you to know that these questions all come up in my mind and that until now, although I see your great effort to assist us, that it at this moment raises more questions than it answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I mean -- I have no meaning to resist the questions that Your Honour has raised --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand. But in the spirit of discussion, I think the questions that Your Honour raised is precisely what I'm trying to bring to the surface.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's see to what extent you manage to do so. I just want you to be aware - I think that's fair - if certain questions arises in our minds that you're aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I appreciate that, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us go back and continue on this and stay with -- and go to page 548213 of the same document, And let us look at Licki Osik, which is approximately halfway down by the Otocac team. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And in that insert you have 2.000 buildings with 250 totally damaged and 7 -- excuse me, 550 partially damaged for 800 buildings damaged. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And now let's go back to the census -- excuse me, 1D190006. And I believe you have a paper copy of that. And in the grid reference that you have, the square-kilometre grid reference of 2.000 buildings, I would ask you to look at the top of the page, four pages in, and you see Licki Osik?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And in that it reflects a number of 953 total structures, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you have listed in yours double those structures within that grid -- that square-kilometre grid reference, don't you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I have to clarify that. Grid reference does not mean that all of these houses were found within the same one-kilometre-by-kilometre square. It gives -- pin-points out the centre of the area which was covered under that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, let's go -- if we go back to page 1 of this document, P176 -- I'm sorry, I'm back to page 1 of P176. If we just scroll down -- I mean, let's just look, for example, on page 1. All of those grid references are grid references for -- towards the top under Team Sibenik, they were all within a hundred metres by a hundred metres?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean, These are very specific areas that you're talking to?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, but how do you produce a grid reference that covers larger area than, you know, than just 100 by 100? I mean, that was the problem that we were dealing with, and these specific grid references, when you put it on the map they would fall into the centre of the area in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think your document answers that, if we could go two more pages up, and that would be 00548203. And if we could go -- if you see the Borkovice --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brtani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- Brtani. What do you do there? You had multiple grid references --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- which expanded the area of examination?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you had available to you the ability to show larger areas in the grids by simply doing what Team Sinj did, right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us go back to one last item on this and if we can stay on this document and go to 00548213. And let's go to Korenica. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Korenica is also known as Titovo Korenica, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn our attention to -- well, in that particular document you have 3.000 buildings and 3.000 buildings being destroyed within that grid reference of a kilometre by a kilometre, right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us go back to 1D190006, and if we could just go to -- and I think you have that paper copy in front of you - to Titovo Korenica which is ten down. And in the paper copy that is before you where you put 3.000 buildings, in 1991 the census reflects a total amount of buildings of 617, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's it. What is the number below that 600?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: A different village, sir.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two numbers on each of these villages. What is the number below?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The number below is -- it looks like 1.716.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. What does it reflect?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the name of that village?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I mean on top of Korenica there are two numbers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I think the witness is drawing our attention to the fact that we always find two lines --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On each --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- on each -- apparently on each village. And he asks what then we find on the first line and what we find on the second line because it looks as if you are quoting from the first line only.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The document as I have before you, Your Honour, puts on the total, and I certainly will go back and provide what other is in that legend, but it is not immediately clear to me exactly what that document -- that line is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you put to the witness that that says 600 and that would be one out of two lines, then you might confuse the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I would expect you to know the difference between what is the first line and the second line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But even adding those together, sir, let's add those together and it takes us to something around 2.000 --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: 300 some.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Where you have reflected in here 3.000 where every one of? those -- the structures have been destroyed?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the team did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the way, is there any way of getting a better legible copy uploaded because I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will, Judge. I will get a better, more legible copy of all these documents scanned in another fashion and uploaded. It is difficult to see, but that's the best I have right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Anttila, I ask you to take a look at P111. Now? Mr. Anttila, this is a situation report from 20 October 1995, and I ask the usher to go to page 3 at the bottom of the page, please, Other Significant Incidents, Relevant Information. Now, in that area it quotes a Slobodna Dalmacija article of 20 October 1995, a statement of General Cermak concerning the burned and destroyed houses in former Sector South was published: "We have told to the ambassadors that information proclaimed by UNCRO of 22.000 burned and destroyed houses in the former Sector South, in other words, 70 per cent of the objects in this area is completely untrue.' "According to our reports there is a number of 2 to 3.000 houses, not 22.000 houses, General Cermak said." Now, was there discussion -- were you aware of this particular comment by General Cermak?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall if that was brought up to me as it is in this situation report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I know -- generally I know that that was the opinion that Mr. Cermak had, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And was there discussion in the United Nations concerning the validity of General Cermak's claims while acknowledging that houses had been burnt and destroyed, that the number that was being produced by UNCRO was well in excess of what had actually happened?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall such a discussion at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's shift gears to another topic, sir, and I would like to refer back to your statement of -- I believe if I can get the exhibit number correct, I have the actual date. And I'm talking about Exhibit P172, page 3, paragraph 3, and in that paragraph, sir, we are referencing you to a visit you took to Uzdolje concerning an incident that had taken place where several people had been killed. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you were there in November, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in November, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when you were there in November you heard the witness say that the individual that did the shooting had a carabine?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That struck me as odd, but yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It struck you as odd because the soldiers of the HV you thought carried either Kalashnikovs or AK-47s or UZs?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you knew based on your experience that a carabine is basically a hunting rifle?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Likewise, sir -- and that caused you to question whether or not this person was an actual soldier, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let me change topics once again and I'd like to talk to you a little bit about your statements, and I would like to turn first to your 1997 statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might have one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in your statement at page 005831 you talk about restrictions of movement. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I think we got the page wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm sorry, Mr. Russo. It's 00548134. I must have misspoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this is an incident the way you went there and you -- this took place on 15 August of 1995. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the 15 August date --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If you go about midway through. It says --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If you just go down on that page a little bit, if we could just scroll that up a bit -- I'm sorry. It's that paragraph on the bottom. You're talking about going to the village of Zrmanja on the 15th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this is an incident where you note that there was houses burning and soldiers and a bus?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if I take a look at this -- that particular incident that you have in your mind --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have not found it yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's the bottom paragraph on that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Bottom paragraph -- yes, I see it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, that particular incident, that was something that was of significance to you, I take it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let's turn our attention to 65 ter 4703, and that is P115. And as you can see, this is a situation report of that same day, 15 August 1995, and I ask us to move up four pages to 509827.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document has only one page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 65 ter number -- it's P120. Your Honour, by way of clarification while we're pulling that exhibit up, that second line is the population line. So for every village you have the number of structures, and the population is the second line.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can scroll down, just a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You can see in this document, sir, that that is the insert of the nine houses burning on 15 August in the area of Zrmanja. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There's no mention of any soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Likewise, sir, with the actual data compilation that you put together in P68, when you were putting that information together, you didn't include any information about soldiers being in there either, did you? And I'm talking about the summary of human rights violations.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you want to take a look at it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it's not in this report because it's not there. I don't ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, I raise this for you, sir, on the issue of the restriction of movement, and you note in your statement that -- and I go back to P172, that last paragraph on P172, page 548134.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We can scroll down on that page, please. Your Honour, I'm just waiting for the B/C/S to come up. Scroll down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the second sentence in there -- starting with the second sentence -- well, actually, we start from the first. "Speaking about the restriction of movement, I would say that from the middle of August (the date of my arrival) until the end of August 1995 there were occasional cases of restriction of movement. The Croats explained such restrictions of movement by the necessity of conducting so-called mop-up operations, when they were looking for rebels. But very often we had such thoughts that the Croats deliberately put such restrictions just in order to have an opportunity to burn houses and loot them without fear." Now, sir, from the time that you were in Sector South, the UNMOs were -- and you were doing humanitarian or HRAT work, right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That too, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, the UNMOs were tracking troop movements of the HV, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the task that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So is it -- were you being told at the time that part of the task of the UNMOs was to continue to follow troop movements of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were on patrol, that was obviously our paramount job, we.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And your testimony that that was a job that continued even after Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is one of the basic tasks of a military observer, so it continued all the way until the time when the sector was closed down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean, did that include tracking the Croatian army into, for instance, Bosnia-Herzegovina, to see what they were doing there?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be within the area of the -- where the UNMOs were working, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So was -- is it your testimony that the general understanding of the H -- of the UNMOs was that they were allowed to go into Bosnia and follow what the -- or report back what HV troops were doing as the warring factions progressed?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The UNMO operation was not limited to the borders of the fractions inside that area. The UNMO mission was inside former Yugoslavia. It was not only in Croatia or only in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And was that the general understanding --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the general understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Let us move to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one clarifying question. Several times you were asked whether it was your job to track troop movements --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. To report troop movements that would be observed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's exactly what I'm -- what is not entirely clear to me. Tracking troop movements, from what I understand the word "tracking" could be, could be either if you see some troop movements you would follow them and you would see where they go and other -- at least in my understanding, another way of understanding tracking troop movements is that you observe troops moving from A to B, and you observe that they're going from A to B, you stay where you are, and you try to link that information with others who might have reported about similar troop movements between D and E. Now, what -- if you're talking about tracking troop movements, would you just observe what happens or would you actively follow those troops in order to -- well, to find out where they would go, not by a stationary observation but by an active and moving following those troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We would not drive behind a convoy after it. We would observe, for example, a convoy and then we would report it and then maybe some other team would in their area respectively put up a patrol to that direction, for example, where these troops were observed to be moving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So when you answered the questions about tracking troop movements, this is how you understood the question and this the way in which you answered it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn our attention to P170. This is again a UN sitrep from 3 -- excuse me, 31 October 1995. If we go to page 2, and we just scroll up just a bit. That's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just waiting for the B/C/S, I don't know if there is no -- there it is, okay. And going to point D on the B/C/S. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in this -- under "Other significant incidents and relevant information." It says: "UNMO headquarters was informed by reliable UN source ..." Now, who could that be, sir?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. "... that they managed to enter Tito Drvar of the following: Patrol was, when coming towards Tito Drvar from the south, stopped in HV-MP," HV military police, "check-point. Patrol was ordered to turn back to Bosanski Grahovo. Patrol was informed that they need permission from military commander in Split (General Gotovina). "Patrol managed to get into Tito Drvar by another route and observed 10 guns, 6 HV trucks ... all parked in a compound where markings with 141 Logistics Brigade was observed." Now, let me go to 1D190013.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, you see the circles, the circle to the left being Knin; the circle in the middle left being Strmica; and to the right Bosanski Grahovo; and the one on the top Tito Drvar. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Tito Drvar -- and the red line is the border, isn't it, between Bosnia and Croatia?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Tito Drvar is, of course, in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, are you saying, sir, that you or that UNMO patrols or -- let me back this up. Drvar was an area near the confrontation line between the Bosnian Serbs and the Krajina Serbs and the HV-HVO, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And are you saying that UNMO patrols were authorised -- UNMO patrols from Sector South were authorised in October of 1995 to travel into Bosnia-Herzegovina and Tito Drvar to report back on what the HV troops were doing?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the sitrep, it's not clear to me if it was an UNMO patrol that made this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I mean, putting that aside, are you independently saying that UNMO patrols were permitted to do that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a task to report the troop movements, and to my understanding we had authority to also go over to the Bosnian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, are you familiar with the agreement that took place and were the other UNMOs familiar with the agreement that took place between the UN and the Croatian government on August the 6th that permitted the UNMOs or permitted the UN to continue to operate in Croatia and what they were allowed to do? Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's put it on the screen, D28. Now, take a look at this, sir, and if you can just give a read through to yourself. Tell me when you need to go to the next page, sir.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Would you please go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Are you done, sir?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just go -- this particular document allows the UN to monitor and report on the human rights situation, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There is nothing in this report that allows the UN to monitor and report HV troop movements, does it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not mentioned there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let's move on to some other areas just as the last area that we'll be discussing. If we can bring up the P173, 2007 document, which is a 2007 witness statement, paragraph 29. Now, paragraph 29, if we could scroll that up just a bit. You note in there -- in that paragraph that: "We could... see men in military uniforms in the same area close to the burning houses ..."

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In paragraph 30, if we could go to the next page, now note that - and we'll talk about this in a second - that: "In remote areas," in the last sentence: "In the remote areas, the Croatian military was burning and looting quite openly." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, you knew at this time that burning, for instance -- and let's just go to P154 and stay -- scrolling down on that page towards the bottom, there is a mention in this document that looting and burning were being done by soldiers and civilians. Do you see that, sir, on the first page? On the paragraph highlights, the third one -- the second one down.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you received reports that the soldiers and civilians were looting together, right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let us turn to another entry on this document if we can just go up three pages to section E, I believe it's three pages, under humanitarian aspects. Okay. Entry under (a) under Team Podkonje, that was your team, right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this is 19 September. And it notes that on 19 September at 8.20 investigated one house on fire in Knin, gives the grid. "No casualties observed. It is assessed that the house was set on fire by neighbours returning to the area."

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And did you observe that to be a -- or was that a common understanding by many of the -- of the UNMOs that much of this burning was taking place by neighbours returning to the area to exact revenge?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes that happened, but it was not the case in all cases where houses were burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's move down on this page under Team Sibenik in the last line. "Patrol observed men in civilian and uniforms looting the villages."

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, was it your understanding that the soldiers and civilians were looting together?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this report, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, how long have you been in the military?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: How long? I have been in military for -- during my conscript for 11 months, and then after that two years I have spent in UN service as a military person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, the military doesn't normally conduct operations with the civilians, do they?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's turn to the next page of this document, and we just -- this is an entry from the UNMO HRAT reported and it's on the 19th and you start -- you see that entry: "191500 September." Do you see that, Mr. Anttila?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just go down about midway through where it starts: "Earlier"?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Earlier I have been visited by --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Notes "Earlier" -- actually we can go to the line right before because I think it makes sense. "The remaining Serbs state that the area earlier have been visited by HV soldier that behaved in a correct manner ..."

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: " ... but they believe that the uniformed men visiting now are not real soldiers ..."

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: " ... HRAT team when visiting Mokro Polje observed several civilian cars (without registration plates) with trailers being loaded with things looted from the houses. The people looting the houses were both in civilian and military uniforms."

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So with --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, it says HV uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. HV uniforms. I'm sorry. "The people looting" -- I stand corrected. I apologise. "The people looting houses were both in civilian and HV uniforms."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, was it frequent that you were being told by soldiers -- excuse me, by civilians that the people -- that the soldiers that were coming in there they didn't think were real soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were cases when that happened, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In fact, sir, if we go back to your 1997 statement, P172, page 548135, the top paragraph -- I'm just waiting for the B/C/S version, Mr. Anttila. I'm just waiting for the B/C/S. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The top of the page blown up, please, I'm sorry. If we go to that sentence -- and in addition to that, sir, you note in this first paragraph, the first carry-over paragraph on the last sentence: "Croats were burning and looting Serb houses independently on their military activity." You mean independent of their military activity?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So these Serbs -- these soldiers were doing it completely independent of what their responsibilities were militarily, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I have tried to say there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, there were also instances where UNMO teams confronted people in camouflage uniforms that were looting, and when they were -- after they were confronted they stopped, didn't they? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware that they were confronted and then in cases they stopped, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And after confronted by UNMO teams they stopped and went away?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- to my understanding, that happened, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And based on your experience and understanding, soldiers that are conducting operations that they're ordered to do wouldn't stop and go away if an UNMO team came and told them to stop, would they?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let me turn to P162. This is an UNMO report from 2 October 1995, just to get yourself oriented, and if we can go to the third page in, 64 -- yeah. And under iv, towards the top of the page, sir, if you read this with me.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "The ongoing harassment and looting of remaining Serb population the CALO," that would be the Croatian army liaison officer, "informed that HV authorities are aware of the situation with the Serb population. He also stated that Croatian civil police, CRO Civpol, can detain and check all citizens of Croatia including servicemen. Only HV and police members in complete uniform and with proper authorisation can carry weapons. He asked UNMOs to pass all information concerning looting to the nearest police station as soon as possible."

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir -- sorry. Sir, were the UNMO teams who were gathering the information that you put together in your statistical compilations, were they routinely reporting this information to the nearest police station as soon as possible?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my understanding, after this was agreed, that that would be the case what happened, But I have not been in a position myself to do that and to witness it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you don't know whether or not these UNMOs did it either, do you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might have one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have any further questions of Mr. Anttila. I would like to offer into evidence the map of Drvar and other locales, 1D190031.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the one with the four circles on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit D172.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D172 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I would also like to offer into evidence the population census as it regards the dwellings, that's 1D190006.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the whole of that census report or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, it's not, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- just the pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just the pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because I had an opportunity to look at it a bit more closely, and where I was talking about 60 entries, I was just looking at the two pages that were provided to us that was I think page 51 and 53, where you see that the areas -- for example, Benkovac, is subdivided in -- in various, apparently, villages and hamlets. And I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Judge, just by way of correction, I think you're looking at the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, I'm looking at the wrong one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. And then let me just -- are you going to tender that one as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I am, Judge. I just -- for the sake of clarity --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then I'll reserve my -- and again, the other one was -- because I have to find it on my computer so that I know --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's 1D1 -- excuse me, 1D1 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I can't find it under those numbers. I only can find it if numbers have been assigned to it. Perhaps after the break I'll come back to that. There are no objections; however, the Chamber reserves the right to ask for more complete --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or more extensive information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But with this proviso -- now, it just disappeared from my screen what the number was. Madam Registrar, could you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The next exhibit 1D190006 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, the last number you gave.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It was D172.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D172 with this proviso. That was the map.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That was the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And this one, 1D190006, that would be Exhibit Number D173.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D173, and I think Mr. Russo told us already that he had no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D173 with the proviso I just made is admitted into evidence. Next one, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 1D190040, this is the population census, I believe, Judge, that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: With the 31 entries for each --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There are multiple entries attached --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I see there's a -- on the top line we find columns up to 31. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Does it look like this, Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it looks like that. And I think that we have only one or two lines --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I only took two lines out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- translated into English, but that allows at least to read what the columns --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- are about, mainly about --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Population nationalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- population nationalities. Yes. In respect of that one, I see on the pages you provided, which I already said are pages 51 and 53, that the areas are subdivided. For example, I think you quoted from one of the villages of Benkovac, if I'm right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I do believe, Judge, that -- the two villages that I talked about were Lisane and Orlici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just trying to find them. Yes, I think it was Lisane Ostrovicke. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's the same village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the same village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, we have not the full subdivision of Benkovac here, so it makes it rather impossible for us to see how Benkovac is subdivided and to what extent this subdivision corresponds with the subdivisions in the UNMO report. So therefore, at least for the villages you mentioned we would like to have the whole of the area in which it is -- the whole of the area in which it is -- in which this village is mentioned as part of that area, in this case would be Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that we're better able to compare what kind of subdivisions have been made and to what extent there is any correspondence between those.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I will have to look at the other one to see whether a similar request would be there. Just thinking aloud, it almost requires expert analysis of these documents to see to what extent the one is structured or is -- can be compared with the others. Because you made it a -- well, quite an issue during your cross-examination that there were inconsistencies, but inconsistencies just on the basis of a name given in an entry might not be sufficient to draw proper conclusions. We might come back to that. Mr. Russo, I take it that there is some need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have some cross of this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kuzmanovic, we will first have a break. We will -- yes, I think as a matter of fact we have not decided on the last exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that will be D174.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D174 with a similar proviso is admitted into evidence. Then, Mr. Kuzmanovic, could you give us an estimate on how much time you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I hope to be no longer than half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No longer than half an hour. We will then have a break and we will resume at five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Kuzmanovic, who's counsel for Mr. Markac. Please proceed, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Anttila.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, I would like to start by going back to an answer you gave to Mr. Kehoe on page 13 of the transcript, line 11, you were asked about the Zadar-Benkovac municipality, and your answer -- the question was regarding damage prior or before Operation Storm in your evaluation. The answer was: "It was our common knowledge that Zadar-Benkovac team was working on the area, that there were houses that had been destroyed before Operation Storm." I'd like the registrar to please pull up P176 and go to page 00548203. Is that on your screen, Mr. Anttila?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The first two-thirds or so of that page include Zadar-Benkovac; correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And in that Zadar-Benkovac evaluation I've counted the total damage as 1.174 and partial damage of 498 for a total number of 1.672. There is no indication on Zadar-Benkovac as to whether or not any of these municipalities had pre-Operation Storm damage; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And are you aware, Mr. Anttila, that the vast majority of these Zadar-Benkovac municipalities had Croatian populations in them?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So at least as far as damage is concerned, if one were to read this document P176 and infer from it that the damage in it was caused by the HV or by Croatian authorities after Operation Storm, it could be misleading; correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like you on the same document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Kuzmanovic. Was the -- we're talking about teams and municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was the Zadar-Benkovac team competent for the whole of the Zadar-Benkovac municipality, or were other teams also competent for parts of -- I mean, was the area of responsibility for the Zadar-Benkovac team exactly the same as the Zadar-Benkovac municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, explain that then.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Team areas were divided on the map, and they were based on the location where the team was accommodated; and then the area was set out around that area. So all the teams had -- in certain areas they would on the map appear exact borders, but because of the roads and so on, you would have to cross over to other teams' AOR while going to a certain place, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: None of that is indicated on the survey, though, is it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, the survey talks about teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And about villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it doesn't say anything about the area of responsibility of the teams, although they get the names apparently of where they are approximately based, but perhaps it becomes too complicated to further explore. If you want to do that, fine, but it might need some preparation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, the Zadar-Benkovac team, for example, didn't go into the Otocac area to survey, did they?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And the Otocac team didn't go into the Zadar-Benkovac area of responsibility, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So for all intents and purposes, the Zadar-Benkovac team covered the area of Zadar-Benkovac, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So let's go to Otocac, Mr. Anttila, and I've got to find my page reference. It is on the same document, P176. 8213 are the last four numbers. Is that in front of you, Mr. Anttila?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's -- the whole page is Otocac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And is it just a coincidence, Mr. Anttila, or is it a fact that every -- that 97 per cent of the entries are numbers of buildings of Otocac end in a 0 or 5, as in a multiple of 5? Is that a coincidence, or is that just the way the buildings were lined up in those villages?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the numbers that were given by Otocac team. I don't -- I don't know why they are multiple by 5 on this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Those appear to be estimates, don't they?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And estimates that may be rounded up or rounded down; we don't know?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So it's fair to state that at least the page concerning Otocac, the number of buildings, isn't particularly accurate?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a conclusion that you can draw from here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If you look on -- again, back on 8206, going back to Zadar-Benkovac, just Zadar-Benkovac alone which is the bottom third of that page, 100 per cent of the entries are a multiple of 5 for numbers of buildings, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And that's another estimate, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And again, it could be accurate; it's probably inaccurate, either rounded up or rounded down, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There were seven UNMO teams, you say?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: How many vehicles did you have?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the vehicle -- number of vehicles we had in the sector, but basically the teams were supposed to have three vehicles for each team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Three per team?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Per team, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And then how many people would go out in a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be anything from two to four.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
