utterances.text: Were the areas of responsibility here -- when you look at P176 you see Gracac, Zadar-Benkovac, were they all the same in terms of area of responsibility, or were some larger or some smaller?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course the sizes were not exactly the same. They were different sizes, different areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement of 2007 - and the exhibit number escapes me, Your Honour - on page 9, P173, paragraph 47, you note that there were 389 villages and hamlets visited through 4 October 1995, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And how many men -- I'm assuming the UNMOs were all men, were they?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all. We had one female UNMO also with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Of the UNMOs, how many did you have for this task to cover 389 villages through the 4th of October of 1995?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the exact number of UNMOs that we had in the sector at that time, but basically there would be about eight UNMOs per team, so that would come up to about 56 people, and then the headquarters staff, so we would be somewhere around total number of about 70.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So on October 4th you have a total of -- at paragraph 47, a total of 389 villages and hamlets that you visited, and if we go to P176, the last page, there's a total of 414 villages listed on P176 as of November 4th, 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So from October 4th through and including November 4th, there were additional 12 -- 25 hamlets that were visited, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That what comes up from the numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, did I understand the testimony well that there was some double counts?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just -- I'm talking about the document in and of itself, not necessarily including the double counts, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please pull up P63, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if I could come back to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the statement, it says there were so many villages and hamlets visited.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I do not know whether a correction has been made for double counts or whether it was counted on the basis of these documents. Then it would include double counts and then your conclusion that additional villages, because it seems to be a conclusion, were visited during that period of time seems to be a reasonable conclusion, whereas if, however, the double counts were already calculated in the 389 then it's not necessarily that additional villages were visited during this period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll cover that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It raises a few puzzles for me. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, other than P65, if we --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Madam Registrar, if you could pull that up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Other than P65 -- and I'll wait until it comes up before I ask my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you -- yeah, that's right. Thank you. Please pull up P65, Madam Registrar. I'll get back to P63 in a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: P65 is the form that was filled out by each team daily in its review of damages in conducting its survey, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they visited a village, they would fill in a form like this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And this is the only form that we have, is it not, that you're aware of in this entire case that documents one particular survey done on one particular day, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So there are seven UNMO teams, right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There -- each UNMO team is filling out P65, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So if there are -- and P65 is basically the guts of your survey, is it not?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And if we can go to -- back to P63, I'll flip between the two for a moment, and I'll wait until the B/C/S gets up before I ask a question. P63 is dated 17 August of 1995, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And that's 1500 hours, so that's 3.00 in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So you would have started your survey, if at all possible, the next day, the 18th, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And for all intents and purposes, the November 4th report, which is P176, that report was compiled based upon the directive to do the survey in P63, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I've counted the number of days from August 18th until October 31st, and that's 84 days.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So in 84 days of doing the survey and -- you know, I'm not a mathematician, but I'll do my best here. In 84 days, there are seven UNMO teams, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And each team has one form that it fills in to give to you to compile the survey?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. That's not the way it worked out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you tell me how it worked, then.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they visited a village, they would fill in the P65, was it, the form, and hand in for each village. So they did not -- they filed several files like P65.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Per day?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: For one day, for example, that's why P65 was -- the team was told to go back and do it different way because they included in that particular document several hamlets, and it was supposed to be done village by village, and these forms that we received, then, they were kept in the file, and we had a big pile of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. You're holding your hands about a foot --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, okay, maybe one full filing --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Binder --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- binder, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Because it appears -- if we go back to P65.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile I'll put one question. When you're saying -- Mr. Kuzmanovic is counting days. Did you work seven days a week on this task?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: UNMO organization worked seven days a week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Seven days a week.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So no days off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No days off. No Sundays.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: We've got P65 back on, and it appears if you move the document to the right if it's possible -- I'm sorry, the other way. There appear to be holes there where this document was in a binder of some kind, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you said you had a full binder of these UNMO humanitarian rights section reports survey forms that was P65?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the only document that we have from all of those forms is this particular one?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, would an UNMO team fill out this for each village that they went to?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the intention, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So if I went to five villages and I'm an UNMO, I have five of these P65s?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to hand in, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So if I went to one village -- five villages in one day, to be more clear, I would have five of these P65 forms?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So theoretically, if there could be more than one UNMO survey done a day by one UNMO team?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So the -- my original calculation was 84 days with seven UNMO teams and each UNMO team completing one form for a total of 588 forms. It could have been more than double that, correct? You could have had more than 500 of these P65s in your binder?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: How come?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you said that if every UNMO team goes to a village, it fills out one of these survey forms, right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, unless that village has already been visited.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And we don't know that because we don't have these underlying UNMO forms, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So the only record that we have that you base your entire survey on is one particular document, P65?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, I think that that question seems to suggest that the entire survey is based on the one example form submitted by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: No, that's not what I suggest, Your Honour. I suggest that the only underlying document that's the guts of his survey, that he said was the guts of his survey is this one document. There are many of hundreds of others of these documents that we don't have that would enable us to verify the numbers that have been presented to us in the survey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Kuzmanovic, I think you're perfectly right that to verify whether the data were transferred accurately on the database. Even without all the calculations you made, you could have come to that conclusion, isn't it? I mean whether it was 588 or 629 or 432 doesn't make a difference. The forms are not there --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and therefore the forms do not allow us to verify whether the data on the forms were transferred accurately into the database.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Despite on whether there were seven, nine, three UNMO teams, doesn't make any difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will move on to P176, using P65 as a basis. If we'll keep P65 on -- I'm sorry, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, there's a grid reference on P65 of 9390, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Chamber what a grid reference is in general.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general a grid reference is -- on the map the -- where the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we do it the other way. Could we -- if the Chamber would try to tell you what the Chamber understands --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll change it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to be a grid, then you can confirm. It is a map --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a map and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that is divided into squares.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And those squares bear numbers, and the grid references, if they are four numbers, then it's, I understand, a square kilometre, and if you give additional details giving it six numbers, then you are in squares of a hundred metres by a hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please call up, Madam Registrar, 1D190043. Not there? It was -- we were advised it was loaded up into e-court. Let's try through Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I'll direct your attention to the map there where the grid reference is 9390?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It's next to the Plavno municipality there, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, if we go to page 2 of that document, 1D190044, that's obviously a close-up view of that grid, 9390, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in P65 it's noted that in that grid, 9390, there are 263 buildings, of which 207 were damaged believed due to Operation Storm, at least according to P65; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I know this is a satellite image, but it doesn't appear to me on this map that there are any homes in 9390?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, and that is why -- like we discussed yesterday, that particular report was -- asked the team to be more accurate on reporting that. But it ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And that was a clear miss, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a clear miss, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to P176 for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I noticed that on the first of your maps Plavno is located rather close to the WJ9390, whereas on the other map it's just in the right top corner --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of that grid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It is a Google map, Your Honour, so if there is some -- Plavno in either respect -- in either of the photos does not appear within the grid 9390.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do agree, but on different places --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It does --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which surprises, as well, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It is a little surprising, Your Honour, but it is a close-up view, so I'm attributing that to the computer graphic rather than any big margin of error. May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, but just for you to know that it surprises me that on the first picture we find Plavno in the south-western part of the adjacent grid, and on the next one we find it in the north-eastern area. At least that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And at the same time, it could be that the first one refers to what appears to be a village, but at least the location where Plavno is indicated on the map is different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go -- we're at -- Your Honour, I'd like to move this -- these photos in evidence with the -- obviously with the stipulation that Plavno is not in 9390.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The stipulation is different from tendering the document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure. I guess --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because whether Plavno -- it might be - I could not exclude for the possibility looking at it closer - that the Plavno village is rather close to WJ9390, whereas the other grid reference, I have not seen that it bears any other name yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly, and I'll get to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So perhaps the stipulation is a bit early.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour. No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no objection to the document being admitted for purposes of what it's been referenced to in the transcript, so long as there is not some understanding that the objection is somehow -- that a lack of objection is adopting the accuracy of what this indicates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't have a problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Its admissibility. So therefore, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this will be Exhibit D175.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D175 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Back to P176. Back to P176, please, and we'll go to page 548207. I'll just reference the last three numbers from now on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The bottom, roughly a little more than a third of this document, references the area of Plavno, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Is there any grid reference here that is a 9390 grid reference as referenced in P65? I'll reverse that question. There is no 9390 grid reference for Plavno on page 207 of P176, is there?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the same thing for page 208, which is the following page, the first three -- the first three entries are for Plavno, and there is no 9390 grid reference, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, if we look at Plavno, if we go back to page 207, the last four columns starting from the right, it goes Other, Partial Damage, Totally Damaged, Number Of Buildings and that's the column I want to focus on for this moment. If you go to Plavno, the third entry, Bradisi, has the number of buildings blank. It has 0 totally damaged buildings and 41 partially damaged buildings, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: How do you figure a percentage of damage when you don't have the number of buildings in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The same goes for two further entries below, being Markelo entry as two totally damaged buildings, but we don't know how many buildings there are there, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the same thing for the village of Petkovi. It has 22 partially damaged buildings, no totally damaged buildings, but yet we don't even know how many total buildings are there?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So statistically it is not possible using at least the figures you have in P176 to come to an accurate percentage of damaged buildings vis-a-vis total buildings, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That can be stated this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I am correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like you to go to page 208, please. We have the same situation in the Team Podkonje in the Palanka area?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There are seven entries in the top third or so of the page or the top half of the page that have no buildings in terms of number of buildings damaged or -- strike that. There are no entries for number of buildings, yet we have entries for total damage and partial damage, don't we?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And it's impossible, then, to determine a percentage?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, you have made your point. Of course, what would interest the Chamber is what effect that would have on the whole. I mean, if it is 1 per cent of the number of buildings missing, then if we look at the totally damaged and partially damaged, then we could make a further assessment on what impact this has on the totality, apart from of course from the apparent imprecisions which appear clearly. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are 414 total villages, and there are 333 villages with the entry number of buildings left blank, yet showing totally or partially damaged buildings, which is 8 per cent of the total. So I'm sure the Chamber can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This clearly is something the Chamber would expect that the parties could agree upon. This is just analysis of a document. Whether that document is in other respects reliable or not of course is a different question, but at least we have an impression without going through it in detail ourselves. Is that something, Mr. Russo, you check whether you could share the views of Mr. Kuzmanovic in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're happy to get together and do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the other percentage that is not reflected accurately at least in P176, Mr. Anttila, is the fact that the number of buildings that were destroyed prior to Operation Storm are not included in the total percentage and are not taken out, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And we've already shown that there were several entries of buildings in municipalities that were primarily populated by Croatians were destroyed, yet the other column was not marked Damage Prior To Operation Storm, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the parties could also analyse this and see whether they could reach an agreement on what impact this has, then the Chamber would be assisted by interpreting these documents, exhibits which are in evidence, and of course we would have to properly analyse them, and the assistance of the parties would be appreciated in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we go to D171, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have that in front of you, Mr. Anttila?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: We have the yellow arrow on the right which is the form -- excuse me, which is P165, coming from the UNMO teams basically to you at UN Sector South HQ?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is P65.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. If I misspoke, I'm sorry. P65?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Those all came to you, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you told us already that P65 basically is the guts of your statistical analysis, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And we only have one page of all of the hundreds of pages of P65s for the analysis, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We only have one page out of the at least 414 which would be the number of the villages included in the survey, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you already told us that P65 at least was done wrong, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That particular one, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Cermak Defence still same position, no need to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Russo. Yes. Judge Gwaunza would have a question for you first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Anttila. Going back to or referring to the sitreps, daily sitreps, and their reference or references to buildings damaged or burning, can I ask would you know whether in giving those figures they would include, for instance, the number of buildings or structures that may have been burning or that may have been burnt within one homestead? In other words, I'm asking whether if a team visited one homestead where there's a house in other smaller structures outside and they found that the house and the structures were burning, in their reports would they say five structures were burning or would they say one, referring to the homestead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my understanding, the teams were considering houses as houses where people would be living, so they were not considering sheds for the livestock and so on. That was their task anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, I just want to take you back through some of the areas covered on cross-examination, and I'll try to work backwards. Form P65, the data-collection form that we've referenced and Mr. Kuzmanovic has indicated is the only one and clearly is the only one that we here in evidence, you gave that to our office from where? Is that the only one that you kept?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is -- because that was not in the file where the ones that the compilation of the data was kept, so I had -- that was an extra one because it had been -- task had been returned back to the team, so that was not put into the file where the other ones were, and that's how I ended up having that particular one with me instead of it being in the files that were given in to -- in Zagreb to UN organization.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we could please, Madam Registrar, pull up P176, and move to the page ending in 8207.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Anttila, you were asked by Mr. Kuzmanovic whether or not any of these entries indicated the grid square reference WJ9390, and I want to focus your attention on, for example, the entry of Palanka in Plavno, which is I believe the fifth one from the bottom there.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And that entry indicates WJ937930.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you explain how that relates to or if it relates to WJ9390 as a location?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's close to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Is it within it or near it or something like that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: 9390 is by the grid number that is three -- there is a three-number difference between 90 and 93, so that would mean distance of about 3 kilometres in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. You were also asked on cross-examination I believe -- this was pointed out by Mr. Kehoe regarding instances where UNMOs had encountered individuals in uniform looting and that when confronted these individuals simply stopped looting and went away. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you give the Court any idea of the frequency of that type of occurrence as -- in relation to the number of times that individuals in uniform were witnessed looting?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, I would say with the caveat if he knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If you know.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have information how many times that would have happened. It happened on occasions, but there were reports of occasions when there is no mention about what happened after these people were confronted.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did you ever have any discussions with any UNMOs who in fact did intervene in instances of looting?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did, and the reports -- or the discussions led to the conclusion that I just said, that in some cases they stopped, and that's hearsay information that in some cases they did not stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And were you given any specific instructions with regard to whether or not UNMOs should attempt to intervene or not?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the information that we had was that we were allowed to talk to people but we could not physically stop them from doing whatever they were doing because we did not have the authority physically to do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. You were also referred to a sitrep in which it indicated that a Croatian army liaison officer on or about the 2nd of October, 1995, requested information or requested that UNMOs provide information about the crimes they were witnessing immediately to a local police department. Do you have any information about whether or not the Croatian army liaison officers asked UNMOs to do that prior to the 2nd of October, 1995?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any information on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'd also like to just clarify something at -- transcript at page 19, I believe it's lines 14 through 17, and this was -- if I can move to it. You were asked a question in regards to the UNMO damage survey. It says: "Let us turn our attention to -- well, in that particular document you have 3.000 buildings and 3.000 buildings being destroyed within that grid reference of a kilometre by a kilometre, right?" And your answer was: "That's true." What I'm asking you to clarify is, are you saying that all 3.000 buildings were in a one-square-kilometre area?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: What exactly do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean by that that what is true there is that there -- in the report there -- the numbers are correct. The Korenica, which is the case, was considered with that one grid reference to be included in that general area of the grid reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. You were also shown a population census document by Mr. Kehoe, and that population census was from 1991. Was that -- the document you were shown, was that the one you were using with regard to the UNMO damage survey, something from 1991?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this particular list is in a different format.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I believe your - and correct me if I'm wrong - your supplemental witness statement, which I believe is P173, if we could turn to that, where it indicates at paragraph 39, and it is the second paragraph there. I would ask you to take a look at that once it comes up on the screen and tell me whether or not you recall if the survey you looked at was a survey from 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may clarify, Judge. The survey is from the census of 1991, but the book itself is out of Zagreb in 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what we see at the cover page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And with that understanding, are you -- are you indicating -- well, is that the same survey that you used for this particular UNMO damage survey? I'm trying to find out if they're the same document that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says there that, so to say, the official Krajina records, which means that it probably was based on the same information but it was produced in a way that it appeared to be by the former Krajina document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could please pull up Exhibit P62.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Anttila, while that document is being pulled up, you were shown a map which indicated that Mr. Munkelien circled a different area in Knin where he believes the crater analysis that the two of you did together was performed.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And I'd like you to please, if you can, assist the Court in trying to determine which area is correct, and what I'd like you to do is, if you're able and if you have a specific recollection of that particular neighbourhood where you say the crater analysis was conducted, were you familiar with it? Is there anything there that sticks out in your mind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm not clear on the question. Are we asking to redraw the map that we had before after the witness has been shown that Mr. Munkelien picked another location? I mean, is counsel attempting to impeach a prior witness? I'm not certain where we are here, but I thought there is a very clear record to contrast that Mr. Munkelien picked out a location that was different than the location picked out by Mr. Anttila.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Therefore, it's of utmost importance to see whether we have any clue to find out who was right and who was wrong or whether the two of them were wrong, not to say that the two of them were right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And, Madam Registrar, if we could please enlarge the area directly below where it says Knin General Supply, and just a bit more if that's all right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, you'll recall generally directly below where it indicates Knin General Supply, that neighbourhood is where you indicated the crater analysis was conducted, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And what I'd like -- and I understand Mr. Kehoe's concern. I'm not -- certainly not going to be asking him to redraw a certain location. What I'm asking him if there is anything about that particular area if he has a specific recollection of what he saw during that crater analysis that could assist the Court to determine whether it was actually there or whether Mr. Munkelien may actually be correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember that the houses were high-rise apartment buildings, so they had several storeys, and they were of a shape not like a block but different balconies and, you know, parts coming from the direct wall outside and -- so these houses in the middle of the picture, to the best of my knowledge, is the place where we did the crater analysis. I don't know why Mr. Munkelien is of a different opinion, but I'm still saying that to my recollection that was the place where we were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, is there any way that the witness could be more precise because he circled the -- well, not to say a large area, but at least quite an area. Perhaps we could ask the witness to see whether he has any recollection on how they -- I don't know whether you went there coming from your headquarters or returning to your headquarters, but if he would have come from the headquarters he might have any recollection or as to how they drove when crossing the railway, for example. Is there -- do you remember whether it was upon returning --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, we were coming from the direction where Mr. Munkelien circled the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So we came past --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So were --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- the army barracks and then entered the residential house area, and when we drove there, we drove in -- into the -- between the houses, and it was a slope going a little bit down -- downwards going into the yard, so basically if you can -- if you can still enlarge the picture a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I would ask for the assistance of the court usher, and perhaps we can simply produce another map which might indicate his route.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's a possibility, but perhaps we first follow the suggestion of the witness. If someone could put the cursor on this photograph so to see -- if you could guide us, Mr. Anttila, with more precision because you're now not just referring to an area but you are saying that it was between the houses. Could you assist the usher in moving the cursor in such a way that we come as close as to where you think the crater was found.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. If you go directly downwards, stop, a little bit up, about there. That was -- I would say after all this time that probably we were between those two houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I might be mistaken, but it looks to me - but I've never been there - that you're now pointing to an area where there appears some trees between blocks of houses -- oh, no, it all --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These three houses that are in different directions than the ones on the top and on the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any way that -- yes, I see at this moment the cursor being at the beginning of what appears to me to be a row of structures --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- with -- I don't know what's there on the roofs, but might be chimneys or something else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And adjacent to it, it looks as if there's a place with what looks to me to be three rows of trees. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, those are houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Those are houses. Okay. That's fine. So that's one row, that's another row, and there we have three rows of houses.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of apparently irregular shape.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Irregular shape. Yeah. That's one of the things that if I close my eyes and think about that incident I can still remember the look of the houses being about that type.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, do you remember whether you left the road because from where Witness Munkelien indicated the crater impact was going down to the place where you crossed the railroad, this seems to be -- do you remember whether you stayed on that road going to the railway bridge or whether you left that road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, coming past the north barracks and then we turned left towards the -- on the road that I would say goes towards the text "Knin general supply," and then we turned from there to ride into that residential house area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you remember what made you make this detour more or less?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were generally looking for different places. We were going through the area, and we tried to cover area that -- so that we could have some kind of impression of what would have happened, and then you could see that there was some -- in that location you could see that there had been some impacts and shrapnels had hit the walls and so on, and we just got -- to my recollection we just got interested to see what had happened there. There was a car parked outside there, a blue Jugo, which had been hit by the shrapnels and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Have the questions in re-examination raised any need to put further questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it has for me, just briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kuzmanovic. Further cross-examination by Mr. Kuzmanovic:

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, P176, page 207. I'll wait for it to get up. You were asked some questions about the Plavno grid references or the grid reference. Mr. Anttila, can you explain why in Plavno there are out of 250 total buildings listed, 271 are listed as totally or partially destroyed or damaged, meaning that there's more damaged or partially-damaged buildings than there are total buildings?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you realize that your survey, Dead On Population Left And Destroyed Houses After Operation Storm, was used and given to the international community to put pressure and criticize Croatia about these numbers?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When compiling this information, that aim was not information that was -- would have been with us. So we did not compile that information for that reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Okay. Did you come back then and -- after -- did you ever determine that it was used in that fashion?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that we got that information when the reports were sent in that it was used in that fashion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did you ever come back and say, Gee, we never subtracted the amount of the buildings that were destroyed between 1991 and 1995 before Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- could I just follow your arithmetics about the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour, about Plavno.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, about Plavno. Could you explain what --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: On the bottom of page -- the last third of page 207, Your Honour, under number of buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: We have 170 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Plus 80.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: -- plus 80 is 250.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And then if we go to the next page, there are no -- in the first three entries no buildings listed for Plavno.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Then all I did was I added the totally damaged or partially-damaged buildings in the Plavno entries and came to 271.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So what I'm trying to understand your point --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The list --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the point apparently being where you earlier referred to percentages, that you now say how could -- you take into account destroyed buildings where no existing buildings are mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the same point as you made before, that if you do not know whether there is a building -- if, for example, in P etkovi we have 22 partly-damaged buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is a kind of arithmetics, of course. What you're actually says is that you should not rely on a building being destroyed or damaged if you have not counted the number of existing buildings?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because no one would expect that you could destroy a building which doesn't exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Right. And it's hard to figure out what the final percentage is if you don't have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the percentage issue you have dealt with which I think was fully understood, but now you're doing more or less the same drawing out a conclusion from the same shortcoming.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No other questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I would have one question for you, Mr. Anttila, and I would like to have pulled up D83. There we -- it's the picture of the shell with the two persons. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it be enlarged a bit. Yes. Now, you have seen this shell yourself at the time?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I'm trying to see what, I would say, almost this sculpture. What it really is if you put it on the market-place it would be art. Could I have the assistance of the usher with the cursor on the picture. Could it be moved to the bottom of the shell? That's the bottom of the picture but not the bottom of the shell. Yes, thank you. Could you slowly follow the line left up of the shell -- yes, up, the centre of the shell. Yes. Could you now follow further up same direction. Yes. Could you now follow the bending piece of metal. Yes. And now a little bit up to -- yes, up to there. You have seen the trajectory I've chosen on this shell. Now, the very end of it, do you remember whether it -- this part of the shell, whether I have chosen the right direction or the right trajectory, or should I follow the curl which appears - Madam Usher, could you please turn a bit to the upper left, upper left, yes, that one - is that the end of the part I just followed ?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be the end of that part that you just followed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the whole of that trajectory from the bottom up till this point indicated by the cursor at this moment, could you give me on the basis of your recollection and perhaps refreshed by this picture, could you give me an indication as to what the length of that curl and then going down to the bottom would approximately be?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole length of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The whole length up -- down from the end of the curl where the cursor now is, then going down, going up again, and then following the body of the shell up to the bottom of it where we started our trajectory.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I would say that the length would be something like the total length would be something like this, like a metre plus something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A metre plus?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, we learned from the details of the -- of the shells that the one you identified total length, so apart from what part would be destroyed upon impact, would be 83 centimetres, which more or less disqualifies this shell as being of the type you determined. Could you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When doing the crater analysis, the first aim is to define the calibre of the weapon used, and then based on the information that we had that time that calibre could be determined, and I didn't even think about that, you know, when the determination of the rocket type was given out, whether it was this or that type because of the calibre was the main interest in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you were not aware that there were two candidates, so to say, for a 128-millimetre projectile?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were not aware of that at that time?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it was on the basis of the calibre that you determined the --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- shell time?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that answer. Is there any question arising from --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then this concludes your testimony, Mr. Anttila. I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and for answering questions put to you by the parties and by the Bench. Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Anttila out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [The witness withdrew].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would like to deliver a decision. From what I understand, the booths have been provided with the second version of it. The Chamber would like to deliver its decision on the Prosecution's motion for Witness 69's testimony to be heard via video conference link. On the 29th of April, 2008, the Prosecution made an oral motion to hear Witness 69's testimony via video conference link. On the same day, all three Defence teams stated that they did not object to the Prosecution's request. On the 1st of May, 2008, the Prosecution filed a recent medical report for the witness. On the same day, the Chamber reached a decision to grant the motion and informed the parties accordingly through an informal communication. According to Rule 81 bis of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence, a Chamber may order that proceedings be conducted by way of a video conference link if it is consistent with the interests of justice. If the witness is unable to come to the Tribunal, if the testimony of the witness is sufficiently important to make it unfair to the requesting party to proceed without it, and if the accused is not prejudiced in the exercise of his or her right to confront the witness, the test of Rule 81 bis has been met. The examining medical doctor found that the witness, who is in his late 70s, suffers or has suffered from various illnesses and accordingly advised that the witness not undertake any longer trips. Having carefully reviewed the witness's medical report provided by the Prosecution, the Chamber finds that the witness is unable to travel to The Hague to testify. Since the witness is expected to testify about one of the scheduled killing incidents alleged in the indictment, the shelling of his village, and the looting and burning of houses, the Chamber is satisfied that his testimony will be sufficiently important to make it unfair to the Prosecution to proceed without it. Finally, the Defence has not argued and the Chamber does not find that the accused would be prejudiced in the exercise of their rights to confront the witness. Consequently, the Chamber finds that it is consistent with the interests of justice to grant the Prosecution's request to hear Witness 69's testimony via video conference link, and the Prosecution's motion is therefore granted. This concludes the Chamber's ruling on this matter. Are there any procedural issues to be raised at this moment? And parties should keep in mind that we are not sitting next week, so if you don't use the opportunity now, you have to wait for ten days. Nothing, nor of the Prosecution nor of the Defence. That means that -- yes, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I arise at the last minute. I did want to just alert the Trial Chamber. I know the Trial Chamber is aware of the problem that I raised earlier in private session. If the Trial Chamber -- I don't know whose court the ball is in, whether you're awaiting a motion from me, or I would await instruction from the Chamber if it's sufficient. I don't know if you wish to review the documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that the Chamber is informed about the matter. You communicated your problems with the Chamber in a rather informal way, and to act proprio motu on behalf of that information, not even knowing exactly -- what exactly your problem is - I do understand it's about documents redacted - then of course you're not satisfied by receiving redacted documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then of course for the Chamber to act, at least what we would have to know is whether the -- whether the redactions are as such that the Chamber would support further complaints.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore, I think the Chamber would expect you to come with more details than just -- and then perhaps ask the Chamber to further deal with the matter. In what way it the matter could appropriately be dealt with, of course, is still to seen. There are several options, issuing orders, hearing persons. There are various ways of dealing with the matter, and perhaps suggestions from the Defence might assist the Chamber in reaching a conclusion in that respect as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We will file a motion, Your Honour. The reason I raise it is I'm also aware the Chamber every time a document is submitted with redactions raises that issue, as well, so I thought the Chamber may have an interest in it, as well, but I will file the motion and then let the Chamber deal with it appropriately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we can compare with previous experiences in this respect, but to act just on the basis of general information might not be the appropriate way to proceed. You're also aware that if you file a motion that there's a fair chance that the Chamber would not see it for the next ten days. Yes. Although, if there are really urgent matters, at least some members of the Chambers are always available to deal with them, and if that's not possible we still have Duty Judges to deal with matters. Then we adjourn -- and now I have to -- always have to calculate - today is the 2nd of May - until the Tuesday, the 13th of May. Madam Registrar, would we be in this same courtroom? In a courtroom still to be announced, and I think we are sitting in the morning, but I'm not quite sure about that. I take it that you'll find that on the court schedule, and Legal Officer will communicate to the parties whether we are sitting in the morning or in the afternoon and whether we are in -- in which courtroom we will sit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I think it's Courtroom II in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Courtroom II in the morning.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: To be corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we adjourn to resume in Courtroom II in the morning of the 13th unless you receive notice of another courtroom and another time.
